ink.note: Seed 1 of 2. Body text, headings, and the fill of every inverted panel. Detected from the host site's palette when a page builder is present, subject to a 7:1 contrast floor against Paper.

paper.note: Seed 2 of 2. Page and card ground. Off-white rather than pure white; the warmth of the system comes from here.

accent.note: The only hue-bearing token. Interactive affordance only: link hover, CTA border and fill. Defaults to the same value as Ink, so an unconfigured install is genuinely monochrome.

accent-soft.note: Accent mixed 61% toward Paper, for link hover. Identical to Soft until the accent is overridden.

wash.note: Derived: Paper 97% + Ink. Recessed ground, hairline grid gaps, and text color on inverted panels.

line.note: Derived: Paper 89% + Ink. Every border and rule in the system. One pixel, always.

muted.note: Derived: Ink 50% + Paper. All mono labels, captions, and metadata.

dim.note: Derived: Ink 71% + Paper. Secondary prose, biography body, chip text.

soft.note: Derived: Ink 61% + Paper. Tertiary prose and item summaries.

faint.note: Derived: Ink 33% + Paper. Ordinals and placeholder captions — present without competing.

onink.note: Derived: Paper 77% + Ink. Primary text inside an inverted panel.

onink-dim.note: Derived: Paper 64% + Ink. Secondary text inside an inverted panel.

onink-line.note: Derived: Paper 15% + Ink. Borders inside an inverted panel.

display.purpose: The author's name, once per page. The only place negative tracking appears. Size is a per-template decision spanning 34–84px; the frontmatter value is representative, not a cap. Set in the inherited family.

headline.purpose: Section headings such as 'Areas of focus' and 'Latest edits', often over a hairline rule. 24–36px across templates. Set in the inherited family.

title.purpose: Item headings — a focus area, a role in the career history, an article title. 14–20px. Set in the inherited family.

body.purpose: Running prose and summaries, 13–15px at 1.6–1.7 line-height. Measure capped at 58–70 characters. Set in the inherited family.

label.purpose: All metadata — kickers, eyebrows, dates, statuses, read times, ordinals, stat units. Uppercase, tracked 0.08-0.2em, one weight step above body, in Muted, with tabular-nums. Separates from content by case, tracking and weight rather than by switching family.

breakpoints.name: cq-lg
breakpoints.note: Container query, not viewport. Multi-column bodies collapse; sticky rails go static; four-up stat rows go two-up.

breakpoints.name: cq-md
breakpoints.note: Container query. Side padding drops to 20px; display type roughly halves; table-style rows stack.

notes: shadows and motion are intentionally empty: the stylesheet contains zero box-shadows, gradients, transitions and animations. This is provisional rather than doctrinal — the system is open to gaining depth later.

All breakpoints are @container queries against the shortcode root, which declares container-type: inline-size. The system never queries the viewport, because the same shortcode lands in a full-bleed builder section on one site and a ~620px themed content column on the next.
Focus is implemented as a 2px Accent outline at 2px offset, switching to Wash inside an inverted panel. The component snippets' :focus-visible rules match the shipped stylesheet.

Typography is inherited from the host theme by default (--abio-font: inherit); a Typeface setting can override it with one of four system stacks. No monospace and no webfont: the label voice comes from case, tracking and weight, and tabular-nums keeps figures aligned. Component snippets below name a concrete family only because the preview canvas has no theme to inherit from.

narrative.overview:
A dossier is a record assembled about a person: an identifying photograph, filed credentials, a track record, source material with dates attached. This system renders exactly that, and its visual restraint is the argument. Nothing floats, nothing animates, nothing is styled to persuade — because the page's job is to be believed, and decoration reads as salesmanship on a page whose entire purpose is establishing that a named human knows what they are talking about. The evidence is the design.

The register is editorial and factual, but the subject is a person rather than a case file, so the system stays warm rather than clinical. That warmth is carried in the paper (a slightly off-white #fbfbfa, never pure white), in generous line-height on running prose, in real portraits at scale, and in a measure held to 58–70 characters so a biography reads like writing rather than a form field. The mono labels and tracked uppercase supply the archival precision; the prose supplies the human.

Color is not decoration here — it is inheritance. Only three seed values exist, and on a configured site all three come from the host's own palette, with the remaining ten derived from them by mixing. The system therefore has no fixed brand of its own by design, and its identity lives entirely in structure: hairline rules, tracked mono labels, sharp corners, honest empty states, and a rigorously flat surface.
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochrome, derived from two seeds plus an accent that adapt to the host site
Flat by construction — no shadows, no gradients, no motion of any kind
Hairline rules and tonal fills carry every separation
One inherited typeface throughout; labels separate by case, tracking and weight alone
Sizes itself to its container, never to the viewport
Absence renders as less page, never as a placeholder or an empty frame

rules.name: The Two-Seed Rule
rules.body: Only Ink, Paper, and Accent are ever set directly. Every other color is derived from them by color-mix() at a fixed percentage, which is why the whole system re-tones coherently when a host site's palette is detected. Never hardcode a color that could be derived, and never introduce a fourth seed.

rules.name: The Inheritance Rule
rules.body: This system has no brand color of its own and must never acquire one. A literal hex belongs only in the seed declarations and in the @supports fallback beneath them. Everywhere else, use a token.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: A detected Ink is only accepted if it clears 7:1 against the resolved Paper; below that it falls back to the default per channel, keeping a good detected Paper even when the Ink is rejected. Body text and inverted panels both depend on that value, so an adaptive palette may never be allowed to drift below a readable floor.

rules.name: The Label Rule
rules.body: If a piece of text is metadata rather than content — a date, a status, an ordinal, a unit, a field name — it is set uppercase, tracked at 0.1em or wider, one weight step above body, in Muted, with tabular-nums. Case and tracking carry the archival register; a second family is not needed.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Running prose is capped in ch, never in pixels, at 58–70 characters. A biography that runs the full width of a wide container stops reading like prose.

rules.name: The One Name Rule
rules.body: Display type appears once per page, on the author's name. Nothing else competes at that scale.

rules.name: The Container Rule
rules.body: Never write a viewport media query in this system. The page does not know how wide the window is and must not care.

rules.name: The No-Dead-Track Rule
rules.body: Any grid whose children come from a variable-length list adapts its track count to what actually rendered. Empty cells are visible in this system because grids paint their gaps.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is one pixel of Line. Not two, not a double rule, not a shadow standing in for a border.

rules.name: The Inherited Voice Rule
rules.body: Never declare a font family outside the --abio-font token. The page belongs to its host, and a hardcoded family is the fastest way to make it look pasted on.

dos: Do derive every color from Ink, Paper, and Accent. If a value can be mixed, mix it.
Do set all metadata — dates, statuses, ordinals, units, field names — uppercase, tracked at 0.1em or wider, one weight above body, in Muted, with tabular-nums.
Do cap running prose at 58–70 characters using ch.
Do write breakpoints as @container queries against the shortcode root, at 1024px, 768px, and 560px.
Do collapse any fixed-track grid to the number of items that actually rendered.
Do render every image through the shared image helper so the hatched empty frame stays the single fallback.
Do let a section disappear entirely when its content is empty.
Do keep separation to one pixel of Line.
Do give every interactive element a visible :focus-visible treatment that survives on both the light ground and an inverted panel.

Do write base element styles with :where() so they carry no specificity. `.abio a { color: inherit }` outranks `.abio-cta` and silently strips every button of its own colour; `:where(.abio) a` does not.
donts: Don't introduce a fourth color seed, or hardcode a hex outside the seed declarations and their @supports fallback.
Don't write a viewport media query. The system cannot see the viewport and must not act as though it can.
Don't load a webfont, and don't declare a font family outside the --abio-font token. The system ships zero font requests and inherits its typeface from the host.
Don't render an empty frame, a blank cell, or a placeholder value where content is missing — show less page instead.
Don't let Accent carry structure. It is interactive affordance only, and on most installs it is identical to Ink.
Don't use a dashed border for anything but the editor-only missing notice.
Don't mix radii within a single template. Commit to square or to a rounded dialect and hold it across every surface that template owns.
Don't rely on hover as the only signal that something is interactive, and never remove a focus outline without replacing it with a visible one.
Don't reach for monospace to signal technical intent. Column alignment is what tabular-nums is for.
